dedupe_keys.name: digital twin for security management of an athens metro station flexsim

description: This study built a digital twin of a metro station in Athens, Greece, in the FlexSim simulation software to support security management of public space. The model represents points of interest and passenger flows with their parameters and predicts security outcomes under different scenarios; experiments varied surveillance camera configurations and camera angles to evaluate how well the space surveillance set-up detects suspicious behaviour. Coverage: one metro station in Athens. Access: arXiv preprint (2025). Licence: arXiv preprint terms. Caveats: a simulation study; detection performance is modelled, not measured in live operation, and the station model is not published. Outcome: strategic positioning of cameras and adjustment of their angles significantly improved detection, and the twin made it possible to find the optimal camera set-up for each scenario. Simulation uses: layout and surveillance planning for crowded public spaces and stations. Related records: the IPPODAMO urban facility management digital twin and the Love Parade crowd disaster analysis.
